name: Chen Jianxing
current_role: Shareholder associated with Wens Foodstuff Group (per Hurun listing); no current public role found
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2016-2021) as sharing a Wens Foodstuff fortune with Wen Xiaoqiong, one of the Wen family members named as actual controllers of Wens Foodstuff Group (Guangdong pig and poultry producer). No public filings or press found naming a 陈建兴 in a Wens director or executive role.
interesting_fact: Wens grew from a 'seven households, eight shares' rural partnership in 1983 into a company with thousands of employee-shareholders, after introducing an all-employee shareholding scheme in 1986.
notes: Could not confirm identity or role from public sources; appears to be a passive family shareholder rather than an executive. Contact only via Wens corporate channels (website/IR). Very low public profile.

name: Colin T. Moran
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Partner, Abdiel Capital (Abdiel Capital Advisors, LP), New York
profile: Hedge fund manager who co-founded Abdiel Capital with Geoffrey Gentile in 2006 after stints at Goldman Sachs and as a partner at Chieftain Capital. Abdiel is a concentrated, long-term investor and long-time 10%+ holder of low-code software firm Appian (APPN); in 2025 it also took a ~12% stake in Rise Gold (RYES), which is reviving California's Idaho-Maryland gold mine.
interesting_fact: Abdiel has reported as a 10%+ owner of Appian for years, filing more than 40 amendments to its Schedule 13D on the company.
deep_cut_fact: Before running money he trained as a historian and lawyer: a summa cum laude B.A. in History and Economics from Duke, an MSt in Modern History from Oxford, and a law degree from Stanford Law School (Order of the Coif).
notes: Low-profile investor; no published personal or firm contact email found. Rise Gold stake per Form 3 (Oct 2025): https://www.secform4.com/filings/1424864/0001193125-25-261127.htm. Education details from MarketScreener aggregator; worth double-checking.

name: He Qiqiang
current_role: Chairman, Guangdong Chant Group (Changqing Group, 002616.SZ), Zhongshan
profile: Co-founded Chant Group (长青集团) in Zhongshan in 1985 as a maker of gas and heating appliances and components; listed it in Shenzhen in 2011. From 2004 he steered it into environmental energy, and it is now a leading Chinese operator of agricultural/forestry biomass combined heat-and-power plants and industrial-park district heating. Remains chairman; shares the fortune with wife Guo Miaobo.
interesting_fact: Chant Group pivoted from gas stoves and heaters to burning crop and forestry residues instead of coal, and its installed biomass CHP capacity ranks among the largest of China's peers.
deep_cut_fact: Before starting his business in 1985 he was a factory workshop director earning about 100 yuan a month, and his early goal was simply to save 1 million yuan, since its ~5% interest would yield 4,000+ yuan a month (told at a 2023 Yabuli entrepreneurs' forum).
notes: Highly relevant to energy theme (biomass CHP). Active in the Yabuli China Entrepreneurs Forum, which may be a warm route. IR email is the board secretary's office.

name: Xing Jiaxing
current_role: Founder and former chairman of La Chapelle (拉夏贝尔); no current executive role found (resigned Feb 2020)
profile: Born 1972 in Pucheng, Fujian, he moved to Shanghai in 1994, began as a clothing sales agent and launched the La Chapelle womenswear brand, aiming to build a 'Chinese Zara'; it became the only Chinese apparel company dual-listed in Shanghai and Hong Kong (A+H). He stepped down as chairman in 2020 and no longer controls the company.
interesting_fact: During the 2003 SARS outbreak he bet against the downturn and ramped up production; when shoppers returned, deep discounting made La Chapelle a nationally known brand.
deep_cut_fact: He learned his trade at a clothing-design training school for just six months, then worked at a Fuzhou garment firm sewing clothes, staffing the counter and delivering goods by bicycle before becoming a business supervisor. He later built a 1,000-mu cherry-orchard leisure farm (樱园) in his home village of Yangdun, Xianyang town.
notes: Sensitive: lost control of La Chapelle in 2020 after his shares were judicially auctioned, and the company later faced bankruptcy proceedings. Avoid these topics. No current public contact route found; hometown agritourism project may be his current focus.

name: Wen Zhifen
current_role: Chairman, Wens Foodstuff Group (300498.SZ), Yunfu, Guangdong
profile: A member of the founding Wen family and one of Wens' named actual controllers, he rose through the company as vice president, president and vice chairman/CEO before becoming chairman. Wens, born in 1983 as a village chicken-raising partnership, is now one of China's largest pig and poultry producers with revenue above 100 billion yuan. He argues modern agriculture is a high-tech industry driven by R&D.
interesting_fact: Under his chairmanship Wens crossed the 100-billion-yuan revenue mark, yet he has publicly said he does not want the company to 'run too fast'.
deep_cut_fact: He trained in animal husbandry at South China Agricultural University's animal science department, later earned a doctorate-level degree at Sun Yat-sen University, and has been named a National Model Worker and shared a National Science and Technology Progress Award (second class).
notes: Hurun lists the fortune shared with Sun Fen (also a named actual controller). IR email is the board secretary's office. Education/awards from a third-party profile (cnpp.cn) - verify before use.
